title: Writing and argument: academic writing and rhetoric
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Read and analyze arguments, write clear thesis-driven essays, use evidence and citation, revise for concision, and write for different audiences.

blocks.deliverable: Summarize a 1,000-word argument in 150 words without distortion.
Outline an argumentative essay with a thesis and topic sentences.
Integrate three sources with correct citations and no plagiarism.
Week 7 midterm; write a fair counterargument paragraph and answer it.
Cut a 500-word draft by a third without losing meaning.
Rewrite a technical paragraph for a general reader.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Argumentative research essay: pick a debated public question, research both sides, and write an 1,800-word essay with a thesis, evidence, counterarguments and citations.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
